title: Caching strategies
body: Caching is one of the most effective ways to reduce latency and cost in distributed systems. An application cache sits between clients and the database. A CDN caches static assets at the edge. Memoization avoids recomputation within a process. The two hard problems remain cache invalidation and naming things. Time-to-live values should match data volatility: seconds for prices, hours for catalogs, days for static content. Stale-while-revalidate keeps responses fast while refreshing in the background. Semantic caching extends the idea to model outputs: store responses by meaning, not exact text, and serve paraphrases without another inference call.

title: Rate limiting
body: Rate limiting protects shared resources from abuse and accidental overload. Token bucket allows bursts while enforcing a long-term rate. Leaky bucket smooths traffic into a steady flow. Fixed windows are simple but suffer boundary spikes. Sliding windows fix the boundary at higher memory cost. Always return Retry-After headers so well-behaved clients back off gracefully. Per-key limits isolate tenants from each other. Global limits protect the control plane. Load shedding drops low-priority work first when saturated.

title: Database indexing
body: Indexes trade write cost and storage for read speed. B-tree indexes serve range queries and ordering. Hash indexes serve point lookups. Composite indexes follow leftmost-prefix rules, so column order matters. Covering indexes answer queries without touching the heap. Partial indexes shrink size by indexing only matching rows. Monitor unused indexes and drop them. Measure with EXPLAIN before and after every change.

title: Retries and timeouts
body: Every network call needs a deadline. Timeouts bound tail latency. Retries with exponential backoff and jitter handle transient faults. Idempotency keys make retries safe. Circuit breakers stop hammering a failing dependency. Hedged requests race replicas and take the first answer. Budgets cap total retry spend per request. Log every retry with attempt counts so operators can see storms forming.
